start.text: A shingle hard under black rock, and boats hauled up on it in rows: hulls on blocks, hulls on their sides, ribs with nothing left on them. Timber stacked and sorted. Chain in coils. Nothing moves.

Up the shingle stands a long low hall of black stone, its turf roof roped down against the wind. A thread of smoke from the chimney. A line of firelight in a shuttered window. And by the door, slung on a frame, a great horn bound in brass, lashed shut.
The lane-house. Where they swear the masters. That horn's answered every boat that ever came home to this hard.
Somebody's lashed it. Go up and see who. Tell them Oda Farrow's in, and she'd like to know why nobody said so.
